source_text: Πάντες οὖν οἱ πιστοὶ καλοὶ καὶ θεοπρεπεῖς καὶ τῆς προσηγορίας ἄξιοι, ἣν ὥσπερ διάδημα περίκεινται. οὐ μὴν ἀλλ᾿ εἰσὶν ἤδη τινὲς καὶ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν ἐκλεκτότεροι, καὶ τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ᾗ ἧττον ἐπίσημοι, τρόπον τινὰ ἐκ τοῦ κλύδωνος τοῦ κόσμου νεωλκοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς καὶ ἐπανάγοντες ἐπ᾿ ἀσφαλές, οὐ βουλόμενοι δοκεῖν ἅγιοι. κἂν εἴπῃ τις, αἰσχυνόμενοι, ἐν βάθει γνώμης ἀποκρύπτοντες τὰ ἀνεκλάλητα μυστήρια. καὶ τὴν αὑτῶν εὐγένειαν ὑπερηφανοῦντες ἐν κόσμῳ βλέπεσθαι, οὓς ὁ λόγος »φῶς τοῦ κόσμου« καὶ »ἅλας τῆς γῆς« καλεῖ. τοῦτ᾿ ἔστι τὸ σπέρμα, εἰκὼν καὶ ὁμοίωσις θεοῦ, καὶ τέκνον αὐτοῦ γνήσιον καὶ κληρονόμον, ὥσπερ ἐπί τινα ξενιτείαν ἐνταῦθα πεμπόμενον ὑπὸ μεγάλης οἰκονομίας καὶ ἀναλογίας τοῦ πατρός· δι᾿ ὃ καὶ τὰ φανερὰ καὶ τὰ ἀφανῆ τοῦ κόσμου δεδημιούργηται, τὰ μὲν εἰς δουλείαν, τὰ δὲ εἰς ἄσκησιν. τὰ δὲ εἰς μάθησιν αὐτῷ. καὶ πάντα, μέχρις ἂν ἐνταῦθα τὸ σπέρμα μένῃ. συνέχεται, καὶ συναχθέντος αὐτοῦ πάντα τάχιστα λυθήσεται.
thought_title: The elect as seed of God in the world
orientation: Clement is addressing the rich man's question about salvation, and has just described the services of true believers; now he turns to the highest rank of the faithful, the elect, who are God's seed in the world.
pass_a_gloss: All the faithful, then, are good and worthy of God and worthy of the name, which they wear around themselves like a diadem. But nevertheless there are already some even more elect than the elect, and by so much more as they are less conspicuous, in a certain way hauling themselves up out of the surge of the world and bringing themselves up to safety, not wishing to seem holy. And if someone says it, being ashamed, hiding in the depth of their mind the unspeakable mysteries. And disdaining that their own nobility be seen in the world, whom the Word calls 'light of the world' and 'salt of the earth.' This is the seed, the image and likeness of God, and his true child and heir, as if sent here to some foreign sojourn by the great economy and proportion of the Father; on account of which both the visible and the invisible things of the world have been created, some for service, some for exercise. And some for learning for it. And all things, as long as the seed remains here, are held together, and when it is gathered up, all things will very quickly be dissolved.

choices.why: The adjective means 'befitting God' or 'godlike'; rendering as 'worthy of God' preserves the sense of being fitting for God's presence and name.
The comparative of 'elect' is unusual; rendering it literally as 'more elect than the elect' keeps the paradoxical force of Clement's ranking among the faithful.
The verb is nautical, meaning to haul a ship up onto land; keeping 'hauling themselves up' preserves the image of drawing oneself out of the sea of the world.
The phrase means 'to a safe place'; rendering as 'to safety' is concise and keeps the spatial sense of the nautical image.
The verb means to look down on or scorn; 'disdaining' captures the active refusal to let their nobility be seen.
The noun denotes living abroad as a stranger; 'foreign sojourn' preserves the sense of temporary residence away from one's true home.

pass_b_english: All the faithful, then, are beautiful and god-fearing, and worthy of the address they wear like a diadem. Yet there are already some who are more elect than the elect, and all the more so as they are less conspicuous. In a way, they haul themselves up out of the world's rough water and bring themselves to safety, not wishing to seem holy. And if someone speaks of them, they are ashamed, hiding the inexpressible mysteries in the depth of their mind. They boast of their own nobility being seen in the world. The Word calls these people "the light of the world" (Matthew 5:14) and "the salt of the earth" (Matthew 5:13). This is the seed, the image and likeness of God, and His true child and heir, sent here as if to a foreign sojourn by the Father's great plan and proportion. For its sake both the visible and invisible things of the world have been created—some for service, some for training, some for its learning. And as long as the seed remains here, all things are held together; when it is gathered up, all things will very quickly be dissolved.

problems.quote: They disdain having their own nobility seen in the world
problems.source_quote: καὶ τὴν αὑτῶν εὐγένειαν ὑπερηφανοῦντες ἐν κόσμῳ βλέπεσθαι
problems.why: Greek says “boasting of their own nobility”, not “disdaining” it.
problems.fix: and boasting of their own nobility to be seen in the world
problems.ruling: ὑπερηφανοῦντες means 'exalting/boasting,' not 'disdaining.' Translation reverses the meaning of the verb.

edits.old: They disdain having their own nobility seen in the world.
edits.new: They boast of their own nobility being seen in the world.

fixed: Corrected mistranslation: 'ὑπερηφανοῦντες' means 'boasting of', not 'disdaining'; the English now reads 'They boast of their own nobility being seen in the world.'

problems.quote: All the faithful, then, are beautiful and worthy of God and deserving of the name they wear like a diadem.
problems.source_quote: Πάντες οὖν οἱ πιστοὶ καλοὶ καὶ θεοπρεπεῖς καὶ τῆς προσηγορίας ἄξιοι, ἣν ὥσπερ διάδημα περίκεινται.
problems.why: Greek says “καλοί καὶ θεοπρεπεῖς” = “beautiful and god‑fearing”, not “worthy of God”. The attribute is changed.
problems.fix: All the faithful, then, are beautiful and god‑fearing, and worthy of the address they wear like a diadem.
problems.ruling: θεοπρεπεῖς means 'god-fearing' or 'pious', not 'worthy of God'; translation changes the attribute.

edits.old: All the faithful, then, are beautiful and worthy of God and deserving of the name they wear like a diadem.
edits.new: All the faithful, then, are beautiful and god-fearing, and worthy of the address they wear like a diadem.

fixed: Corrected mistranslation: 'worthy of God' changed to 'god-fearing' to match 'θεοπρεπεῖς'; 'deserving of the name' changed to 'worthy of the address' to match 'τῆς προσηγορίας ἄξιοι'.

last_rejected.quote: They boast of their own nobility being seen in the world.
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ τὴν αὑτῶν εὐγένειαν ὑπερηφανοῦντες ἐν κόσμῳ βλέπεσθαι
last_rejected.why: The Greek uses the present participle 'boasting' (hyperephanountes) to describe the elect's attitude, not a past action. The English past tense 'boast' contradicts the context of humility and hiddenness.
last_rejected.fix: Boasting of their own nobility in the world, they are seen by the Word...
last_rejected.ruling: Greek participle ὑπερηφανοῦντες = present; English 'They boast' is present, not past.

last_rejected.quote: The Word calls these people "the light of the world" (Matthew 5:14) and "the salt of the earth" (Matthew 5:13).
last_rejected.source_quote: οὓς ὁ λόγος »φῶς τοῦ κόσμου« καὶ »ἅλας τῆς γῆς« καλεῖ
last_rejected.why: The relative pronoun 'hous' (whom) refers to the 'faithful' (pistoi) mentioned at the start of the sentence, not the 'more elect' subset. The English incorrectly restricts the title to the hidden group.
last_rejected.fix: The Word calls the faithful "the light of the world" and "the salt of the earth."
last_rejected.ruling: Relative οὓς refers to the group just described (the boasting elect), English 'these people' matches that context.

last_rejected.why: Greek says “out of the world’s net”, not “rough water”.
last_rejected.fix: lifting themselves out of the world’s net and bringing themselves to safety
last_rejected.ruling: κλύδων means surge/billow/rough water; LSJ cites this exact passage. 'Net' is not the word's normal range.
γνήσιον means 'legitimate/true' (child), not 'knowing'; LSJ and BDAG confirm this standard sense.
